V22_FSE_receive.  The window clamp and the history shift are exactly the
shape a separating-trial counter gets wrong -- a clamp downstream can take
two readings to the same result on the inputs that separated them upstream --
so each is written out here and run rather than rested on a counter.

label: the window is not clamped while the history is still filling
the window clamp uses >= where the object uses >
why: EXPECTED UNCAUGHT, and it is an argument about the code rather than about the suite: `hist_n` is never 48 at this site, so `>` and `>=` agree on every input. Proof in two parts. (1) After a shift, `hist_n_new = hist_n_old - 49 + need` and the shift only fires when `hist_n_old + need > 98`, so `hist_n_old >= 99 - need` and therefore `hist_n_new >= 50`. Every post-shift value is at least 50. (2) Before the first shift `hist_n` runs 1, 7, 13, ... -- one for the first symbol then six a symbol -- and 48 is not of the form 1 + 6k, since 47 is not divisible by six. So 48 is unreachable from either direction. Simulated as well, over whole-symbol drives and over ragged ones that split symbols across calls at every offset: 58 distinct values occur at this site, the ones below 50 are exactly {1,7,13,19,25,31,37,43,49}, and 48 is not among them. THE COUNTER THAT USED TO STAND FOR THIS DID NOT SHOW IT. t_v22recv counts `window clamp 16 / full window 784`, which separates a clamped reading from an unclamped one -- that mutation IS caught -- and says nothing about the boundary of the comparison. Two different claims, one counter.
